text:
Alex: quick sync — I'm proposing a new 'safety-net' guard for rollouts to protect against sudden token-cost spikes and tail latency regressions.
Mira: curious — how is this different from the autopause/guard we already have?
Alex: good q. current autopause is global and reactive (based on aggregated token burn and error rate). safety-net would be tenant-scoped, configurable per-rollout, and support non-blocking notifications + optional soft-diversion.
Jonatan: +1 for tenant scope. we've had a large customer hit a surprise token surge from a bad prompt change.
Sam: what metrics do we want in the guard condition? SLOs (p50/p95 latency), 5xx rate, and projected token burn over next hour?
Mira: projected token burn is tricky. need a simple estimator in the control plane that uses request rate * avg tokens in last 5m.
Linh: can the estimator respect sampling for streaming? we only sample some streaming sessions atm.
Alex: yes, estimator should use both completed responses and sampled streaming deltas. keep it conservative (use 95th percentile estimate) to avoid underestimates.
Jonatan: config API idea:
```
{ rollout: { traffic_percent: 10, guards: [ { type: "safety_net", scope: "tenant", conditions: [ { metric: "p95_latency_ms", op: ">", value: 500, window_sec: 300 }, { metric: "token_rate_per_min", op: ">", value: 20000, window_sec: 600 } ], actions: [ "notify", "soft_divert: 50%", "pause_if_persist: 900" ] } ] } }
```
Sam: I like actions being composable. soft_divert should be a first-class action that routes a percentage to baseline model or a cheaper quantized variant.
Mira: UX in Console: we need a succinct summary card with current guard state, last trigger time, and the projected cost impact if we continue.
Alex: agree. telemetry needs to surface "what-if" projected spend after applying the estimator. that helps SRE/Sales decide whether to approve.
Jonatan: on pause semantics — do we hard pause (stop traffic) or reduce to a failover model? hard pauses can break user flows.
Linh: prefer staged approach: notify -> soft divert -> throttle (rate-limit) -> pause only if persists. each stage configurable thresholds.
Sam: should default policy be conservative? ex: for paid tenants with SLA we slow first, for free-tier we can be more aggressive.
Alex: yes defaults by tenant tier. keep explicit overrides allowed in rollout YAML.
Mira: telemetry events: guard_evaluated, guard_triggered, guard_action_taken, guard_recovered. include context: rollout_id, tenant_id, window_metrics, estimated_hourly_burn.
Jonatan: add debug payload for troubleshooting (sampled request ids) but only in internal logs (PII safe).
Alex: deploy-bot: rollout check completed for branch safety-net-proposal.
deploy-bot: CI passed: 12 tests, 0 failures.
Linh: we should also expose a dry-run mode where guard logs what it WOULD do without taking actions. helps teams test configs.
Sam: +1 dry-run. console could have a 'preview' toggle in rollout create flow.
Mira: UX question — how to present recommended guard values? Maybe a button 'auto-suggest thresholds' that runs historical-profile on selected tenant.
Alex: auto-suggest is great. we'll limit to 90-day historical window and present suggested p95 latency and 5x normal token_rate.
Jonatan: who owns the rollout API change? I can take the server side evaluator and estimator. Linh can own sampling integration. Mira do console cards, Sam telemetry. Alex will write a short design doc.
Alex: plan: I'll open a PR with API schema + design doc link and a spike for estimator by EOW.
Mira: sgtm. add me for console review.
Sam: I'll draft telemetry event spec and retention policy (we might want 90 days for per-rollout analysis).
Linh: will add sampling flags and make sure streaming delta calculation is resilient.
Jonatan: one more: add a 'rollback recommendation' hint when guard triggers multiple times in a short window (like 3 triggers in 15m).
Alex: good call. include that as a soft hint, not automatic rollback.
Mira: ok let's track this in the rollout guards RFC board. link when PR is up. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks team — logging the action items in the PR.
Sam: leaving a note for security: ensure sampled request ids are redacted in tenant-facing UI.
Linh: noted.
Alex: last: any objections to adding 'cost_per_token_threshold' as explicit metric? helps customers set monetary guard instead of token rate.
Jonatan: yes include cost_per_token_threshold and currency. multi-currency edge cases later.
Mira: sounds good. end state: tenant-scoped safety-net guard, dry-run, staged actions, console preview, estimator/autosuggest.
Alex: ok closing thread — will post PR link shortly.
